summary: Correct Core-private selection of the newest applicable eject-cleanup provenance on same-pool rejoin. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: The existing same-pool rejoin workflow remains correct; this restores its durable provenance selection.

api.reason: Core selects existing managed-journal provenance differently without a route, request, response, or schema change.

roadmap.reason: The pending correction does not complete S7 or Phase 4 acceptance.

state.reason: Core owns eject-cleanup provenance and its reapply-consumption lifecycle.
state.record: Existing managed-journal cleanup provenance carries the resource and membership generations used to select a one-use reapply grant; Core inventory remains the adoption path for a replacement Controller.

verification.method: A preserved disposable fixture contains two marked eject cleanups at the same resource generation and different membership generations. The older receipt was consumed while the later removal remained effective. The newest-membership selection correction is independently reviewed. Its multi-cycle regression covers newest provenance selection, tied-generation fail-closed behavior and real media receipt projection; a resource-generation-only negative control fails. Focused, package and race checks passed, followed by the final whole-tree race and 374-test Python source gate. On the reviewed Core delta, ordinary reconciliation consumed the newest cleanup from the preserved journal: the shared repository mounted, the ISO reappeared, and master API read/write, VM runtime, locking and content-digest checks were healthy. An intentionally unmarked later network removal remained absent. The fixture was not repaired in place. This is bounded preserved-journal recovery, not a fresh full eject/rejoin cycle or Phase 4 acceptance.
